statements.quote:
To address this gap, our study examines the impact of generative AI on team performance 
and processes through a preregistered1, randomized controlled experiment.

In our first experiment,2 conducted within a controlled behavioral laboratory setting (see 
Supplementary Materials3), we sought to elucidate the dynamics of generative AI integration and 
team performance by having participants engage in a series of professional tasks.
statements.locator: p. 8, Section 2.1, Experiment I, laboratory-setting supplement pointer

statements.quote:
Each task was selected for its relevance, as 
well as its varying levels of complexity and creativity requirements, thereby providing a 
comprehensive view of the participants’ abilities in collaborating with AI (further task details 
provided in Supplementary Materials).

Prior to the start of the experiment, participants were required to complete a personal 
background questionnaire, which collected a wide range of personal data including demographic 
information, IQ, and previous experience with generative AI.

After completing the initial tasks, participants filled out a post-
experiment questionnaire to capture their perceptions towards team processes, including team 
coordination, potency, information elaboration and satisfaction (see Supplementary Materials).

Furthermore, chat log files were extracted from ChatGPT4.0, capturing their interactions with 
the generative AI, which detailed all prompts and step-by-step responses of participants, 
providing data for further analysis of the mechanisms underlying human-AI interaction.

Each task output was evaluated based on three dimensions: overall quality, novelty, and 
usefulness (Amabile, 1983), rated on a scale from one to ten (see Supplementary Materials).

Participants 
completed the same identical questionnaire to gather personal data before the tasks.
statements.locator: p. 11, Section 2.2, reuse of the questionnaire

statements.quote:
Human input was also assessed utilizing the GPT-4.0 API, known for its robust text 
understanding capabilities (Dell’Acqua et al., 2023). From a depth-based perspective, the most 
impactful human-AI interactions may stem from the deepest engagement, where team members 
leverage AI’s capabilities to the fullest extent. Therefore, to capture the effect of deep 
engagement, we selected only the top 25% of prompts by score to construct a human input 
indicator (detailed methods and measurements can be found in Supplementary Materials).
statements.locator: p. 19, Section 3.2.7(1), Interaction Indicators, supplementary methods and measurements

deposits.notes:
Group AI. The paper's published view_only URL permits anonymous access without an account, so access is coded public. The node metadata itself says public=false; retaining the published view_only parameter is necessary for reproducing this check. Landing page, node metadata, storage-provider listing, osfstorage file listing, children listing, and linked_nodes listing all returned HTTP 200 with that parameter. There is one storage provider, seven root files, no folders, no children, and no linked nodes.

Dataset_study1.dta was downloaded into memory from https://osf.io/download/ea3z2/?view_only=ca644891d4234935b1464fbc20ce6e85 (HTTP 200; 39776 bytes) and read with pandas.read_stata. rows_checked and columns_checked refer to this confirmed S1 file. Its 244 rows are 122 distinct team_id values times two tasks, with unique team_id/task pairs and no missing arm or outcome values. A denotes multiple-AI (78 outputs, 39 teams), B single-AI (82 outputs, 41 teams), and C1 human-only (84 outputs, 42 teams), confirmed against ai/single_ai/multiple_ai. All nine arm outcome means and SDs reproduce the saved PDF's Appendix A Table 1 (p. 34) to its printed precision.

The schema has no team-output-level category. aggregate_only here means outcomes and covariates at the team level: the file contains individual team-task output rows, not merely arm summaries. team_id is not an individual participant ID. There are no participant records, individual-level questionnaires, raw judge-level ratings, original task outputs, prompts, responses, or semantic-diversity values. Its only string fields are team_id and task_type. Team arm and size are constant over tasks. Summing team_size once per team gives 435 represented team members: human-only 142, single-AI 150, multiple-AI 143, pooled AI 293. These are calculations from analyzed teams' size fields, not independently checked person-level participation/exclusion records.

Dataset_study2.dta was also downloaded and read entirely in memory from https://osf.io/download/xubav/?view_only=ca644891d4234935b1464fbc20ce6e85 (HTTP 200; 99287 bytes): 674 rows and 30 columns. Columns: company_id, group_id, task, task_id, task_type, overall, novelty, usefulness, ai, single_ai, multiple_ai, team_age, team_gender, team_education, team_iq, team_ai_use, team_size, team_familarity, team_job_rank, team_average_subordinates, std_team_age, std_team_gender, std_team_education, std_team_iq, std_team_ai_use, std_team_size, std_team_familarity, std_team_job_rank, std_team_average_subordinates, ai_size. It contains team-task ratings with company/group identifiers and three team arms (Human, Single_AI, Multiple_AI), not the saved paper's 139 individual-AI participants and 278 individual outputs. All team_size values are 3-7. Current Appendix.pdf p. 3, Table A4, reports Study 2 N=674 with company effects; p. 4 describes 15 organizations. These materials establish a different team-study scope. Do not equate the deposited 'study2' filename with form study S2. S1 data also supply the team comparators reused in S2, but no original S2 individual data were found.

All seven files were fetched successfully (HTTP 200), below 20 MB each, and inspected in memory; no downloaded file was saved. Supplementary Materials.pdf has 31 pages: original tasks and rating rubrics labeled Pilot Study on pp. 1-6; later company-specific tasks beginning p. 7; interaction-log processing and diversity methods on pp. 30-31. Appendix.pdf has seven pages of aggregate tables/methods/figures. They are materials and aggregate results, not participant texts. The three scripts are analysis code, not data. step1_cache_embeddings.py and step2_calculate_diversity.py require interaction_records.xlsx and embeddings_cache.pkl; neither is in the seven-file listing. The code expects prompt text and research_ID, which are absent from both DTA files. Therefore diversity measures cannot be computed from the deposited files.

Repository files postdate the saved paper: both DTA files were uploaded 2025-03-11, Supplementary Materials.pdf 2025-03-12, and the three scripts plus Appendix.pdf 2026-02-11. The repository's changing Study 2 scope prevents assuming that its current materials reproduce all parts of the May 2024 paper. No dataset/project license was present in the returned project metadata or seven-file inventory; license is null.

Public preregistration titled 'Exploring the Influence of AI Accessibility on Group Creativity', registered 2023-09-23. The landing page returned HTTP 200. Initial /v2/nodes/5su8c/ and /children/ requests returned HTTP 404 because this identifier is a registration, not a project node; /v2/nodes/5su8c/files/osfstorage/ returned HTTP 200 with zero files. Correct /v2/registrations/5su8c/ metadata, files/osfstorage, children, storage-provider, and linked_nodes endpoints all returned HTTP 200 with the paper's view_only parameter: zero files, zero children, no linked nodes, and only osfstorage as a provider. This is not a dead link. The registration's structured responses contain design, hypotheses and planned outcome definitions, not observations or realized assignments. It lists Creativity of Task Performance and several team-process outcomes; it does not explicitly designate one primary outcome. The license relationship was followed to /v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e972/ (HTTP 200), confirming MIT License. That license applies to this registration; it is not assumed to license the separate zq48w data.

Related later research lead, not a confirmed deposit for any original form study. DataCite's author-plus-topic search returned doi:10.17605/osf.io/p8b59, 'Examining the Impact of Generative AI on Team Performance', by Ning Li, registered 2024-07-15. The protocol targets more than 1500 employees in human-only, single-AI and multiple-AI teams and says data collection was ongoing. Its date and team design do not match the saved May 2024 paper's Experiment II individuals. Landing page, /v2/registrations/p8b59/, files/osfstorage, children, storage-provider and linked_nodes APIs all returned HTTP 200. There are no files, children or linked nodes, only structured preregistration material. The license API /v2/licenses/563c1cf88c5e4a3877f9e965/ returned HTTP 200 with name 'No license'; license is null. It supplies no additional participant-level data.

what_we_could_compute: For S1-O1/S1-O2/S1-O3, average the two task ratings within each team_id and compute arm means, SDs and SEs across independent teams, including the pooled-AI arm. The task-level file also allows outcome-specific counts, task-specific summaries, and team-clustered regression SEs using its arm indicators and covariates. This addresses final.open_items on independent-unit precision for Experiment I; these are team-level, not per-person, estimates.

For final.open_items on Experiment I analyzed headcounts and reused team comparators, sum the exact team_size field once per analyzed team_id: 435 members represented overall, 142 human-only, 150 single-AI, 143 multiple-AI, and 293 pooled AI. These derived counts improve on the rounded table means but cannot independently verify person-level attendance/exclusions or identify overlap with Experiment II.
notes:
Checked 2026-10-09. Read the complete 92,689-character markdown in successive chunks, through both Appendices A-B and the final figures (55-page saved PDF). Checked relevant PDF pages with PyMuPDF, including all supplement/preregistration pointers, original Experiment II description, and Appendix A Table 1. Statements are extracted verbatim from the saved PDF, retaining extraction line breaks and footnote numerals; collection/acknowledgment statements do not imply a promise to share data. No explicit data-on-request, open-data, analysis-code, or separate data-availability statement appears in the saved paper. The form's data_and_code has empty data_url and code_url values.

Classification follows the brief's strict participant-level criterion. Public data confirm S1 arm assignments and output scores at the randomized team level, but no individual participant IDs or participant-produced texts/ideas. Consequently public_participant_data is not justified. The missing interaction_records.xlsx/embedding cache prevents diversity calculations even though diversity-analysis code is present. Original S2 individual-AI data, person-level means/SDs/SEs, cross-experiment participant overlap, and S2 recruitment composition cannot be recovered from the inspected files. Neither DTA has a task-completion-time field, so time-controlled analyses and their p-value conflict cannot be checked from them. The deposited code/materials are later than the saved paper and do not establish which conflicting original Bayesian estimates the authors intended.

The original preregistration and current external supplement are now accessible, resolving the prior screeners' access failure, but their availability should not be mistaken for complete original participant data. The current supplement describes later diversity methods and team-study material rather than the saved paper's full human-input/time/individual-AI analyses. The arXiv landing page currently identifies only v1 (2024-05-28); the current OSF additions are not evidence of a newer arXiv version. SSRN's bot check prevented assessing a later SSRN or publisher supplement.

Besides the two OSF links, the markdown contains three URLs in references to other papers. Each was requested after stripping trailing sentence punctuation: https://scholarspace.manoa.hawaii.edu/handle/10125/59469 returned HTTP 200; https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4573321 returned HTTP 403 with a bot check (stopped); https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10565103/ returned HTTP 200. These are not c446 data deposits. No other repository URL occurs in the saved markdown/PDF. Relevant search leads were checked without login or access requests.

Searches used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1. No general web-search tool was used. Author-name searches can return namesakes and title-substring false positives; the broad DataCite first-author search was only partly inspected and was supplemented with a complete 21-result author-plus-topic search. A negative search result is not proof that no other deposit exists. Confidence is high in the confirmed public-partial classification and the inspected file contents; the connection of the later p8b59 protocol to a revised manuscript remains unconfirmed.
